notes: The session's web-search allowance ran out after eleven searches, so most candidates got no search at all, only direct page reads with the kit's honest User-Agent (official court and school district pages, the Michigan Manual, Wikipedia, named news organizations). No campaign website was found for anyone; none was guessed.

Left out and not worked around: michigan.gov answers scripts with 403, so the Governors' appointment releases for David J. Allen (2003), Shannon A. Holmes (2011) and Jennifer Smith Deegan (March 19, 2024) could not be opened. Deegan's appointment to the St. Clair County Probate Court (a partial term from April 8, 2024) was read only on a lobbying firm's news page, which is not a kind of source the rules allow, so no office is recorded for her; a later pass with search could use the county's or a newspaper's page.

LaMar D. Lemmons (Detroit school board): Wikipedia and the 2005-2006 Michigan Manual describe LaMar Lemmons III (State Representative 1999-2003 and 2005-2007, later on the Detroit Board of Education), but his father of the same name also served in the Legislature and nothing opened ties the candidate's middle initial to either man, so nothing is recorded.

Andrew Beeler's birth year on Wikipedia is marked 'citation needed' and is left out. Chris Christenson: an East Village Magazine report of August 2018 shows him in that year's primary for the Genesee circuit bench, but no page opened states the year he took the bench, so the year is blank. Bruce de Wit: the City of Walker's news page names Mike Burde as the commissioner appointed to the Ward 1 vacancy in January 2026; nothing about de Wit was found.

Sitting legislators Stephanie A. Young, Thomas E. Kuhn and Michael Webber: no campaign site could be opened (the address Wikipedia gives for Young did not resolve) and no party endorsement page was found. Nothing found beyond the filing for Michael E. LaBuhn (aggregator pages only), Paul Ledford, Jennifer Deegan, Dianne E. Cotter, Jennifer Barnstable, Tommy Doles, Angela Schultz, Tom Braun, Brian Hayes, Austin L. Aamodt, Brynn Stevenson, Lula R. Woodard, Kathi Kobeissi Martin, Jody White, Angela M. Jones, Jennifer Long and Briar Bearss; their districts' board pages, where they opened, did not name them.
